item.title: Abdul El-Sayed's resurfaced kiddie show campaign clip ripped to shreds in brutal internet takedown
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed's bizarre "Blue's Clues" Senate campaign video went viral, drawing widespread mockery online and a stunned reaction from Ted Cruz on X.
item.content:encoded:
The internet is ripping apart far-left Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed after a bizarre "Blue’s Clues" themed campaign video resurfaced, pleading for votes while dancing and singing along to a jingle from the children’s show.

The clip begins with El-Sayed mimicking the "Mail Time" segment in Blue’s Clues. The candidate for U.S. Senate mirrors the host’s exaggerated dance movements, including a little butt wag, and recites the song. He even dons the signature green-stripe collard shirt.

"Here's the mail, it never fails, it makes me want to wag my tail. When it comes I want to wail, ‘Mail!’" El-Sayed recites at the onset of the campaign video.

EL-SAYED PALS AROUND WITH FAR-LEFT STREAMER HASAN PIKER THE DAY BEFORE CRUCIAL MICHIGAN SENATE ELECTION

The Michigan socialist then pulls out a ballot from the mailbox, which reads "Abdul for Senate," and goes on to explain the details and regulations for turning in a ballot.

"It looks like my ballot," El-Sayed says in the video. "And with it, I can participate in democracy."

He then continues to tell the viewers the dates by which the ballot must be turned in and postmarked to be counted. He did so, however in the same tone as how the "Blue's Clues" host speaks to his child audience.

"Vote ski-doo, we can too!" El-Sayed said while shrinking and disappearing into the "Abdul for Senate" picture frame behind him.

This copied yet another bit from the television series, "Blue’s Skidoo, we can too!", where the host would became part of the cartoon background.

"Um, wut?" Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, posted to X about the video.

The clip went viral on social media Wednesday, with supporters from the left arguing the video is playful campaigning. Meanwhiole, conservatives tore into El-Sayed for being cringe and infantilizing the election process by appearing to intentionally direct to campaign video to children.

El-Sayed's campaign did not respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment on the video.

EL-SAYED DARES GOP RIVAL TO NO-PADS FOOTBALL SHOWDOWN AS SENATE FEUD TURNS PERSONAL

"This is genuinely disgusting and patronizing," one user said. "Treating adult citizens and massive economic issues like a gentle episode of Blue’s Clues is a complete joke. Stop weaponizing our childhood nostalgia for a cynical election campaign. We aren't children, and we want real."

"Could be the worst thing I’ve ever seen in my life," said another.

Yet another user wrote: "Perhaps the most cringeworthy political advert I’ve ever seen. You could hold a gun to my head and I’d still not film this video. What sort of voter finds it appealing to be spoken to like a toddler watching Blue’s Clues?"

"Perfectly appropriate if one believes his voters have the intellect of 4 year olds. It’s so much easier to trick them into socialism at that age.

"No one should be allowed to vote for this," another user said. "Like, no one. Sorry. This cannot be encouraged."

HALEY STEVENS CONDEMNS HASAN PIKER BUT RALLIES BEHIND EL-SAYED AFTER NARROW PRIMARY LOSS

The video was part of the early days of El-Sayed’s campaign.

Now, after narrowly beating moderate Rep. Haley Stevens , D-Mich., in the cutthroat primary election on Aug. 5, the clip has reemerged and gone viral. El-Sayed will go face-to-face with Republican Mike Rogers in the battle for Michigan’s Senate seat in November.

The controversial progressive has campaigned with socialist streamer Hasan Piker, known for saying "America deserved 9/11," praising Mao Zedong and Communist China, arguing that capitalists should be murdered in the streets and spewing a litany of antisemitic bile.

item.title: Scope of CCP-backed Chinese exchange program inside American schools uncovered in sweeping report
item.description: A Defending Education report reveals 83 universities and 26 K-12 schools joined Xi Jinping's exchange program run by a Marxism-Leninism agency.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: Dozens of American colleges, high schools, middle schools and elementary schools have taken part in a program launched by Chinese President Xi Jinping and run by an agency dedicated to promoting "Marxism-Leninism," a new report published by the parents' rights group Defending Education found. 

At least 83 universities and 26 K-12 schools across 30 states have participated in Beijing’s Young Envoys Scholarship, an exchange program which the Chinese Communist Party says is designed to improve relations with the United States, according to the report. Critics, however, maintain that Chinese exchange programs serve a political function, allowing the CCP to curate manicured experiences to unduly sway American perceptions of China.

The program’s reach underscores how Beijing uses educational exchanges to build influence with American students even as U.S. officials, the president among them, are increasingly scrutinizing CCP efforts to shape public opinion and gain footholds in institutions. The new Defending Education report raises questions about what students are shown in China, who shapes those experiences and whether schools and families fully understand the political implications of participation.

HARVARD TOPS NATION IN FOREIGN CASH HAUL AS COTTON DEMANDS PROBE INTO CHINA FUNDING

"The Chinese Communist Party engages in cognitive warfare to distort American perceptions of the CCP‘s endless human rights abuses and global aggression," Michael Lucci, the CEO of the national security nonprofit State Armor, told Fox News Digital. "They are reaching deep into our education system to influence American students as one of their influence operations to try to change the way Americans think."

Xi established the program in 2023 with the aim of inviting 50,000 young Americans to the country over five years.

The China Education Association for International Exchange, which runs the program, uses "Marxism-Leninism, Mao Zedong Thought, Deng Xiaoping Theory … and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as its guiding ideology and action guide," according to a translation of its Chinese-language website.

"These aren't just cultural trips. They're an integral part of China's broader soft power strategy aimed at infiltrating America's classrooms," Reagan Dugan, the director of Defending Education’s higher education initiative, told Fox News Digital. "Disclosure requirements need to catch up. American students and families deserve to know if their school is partnering with a CCP operation."

The Chinese government maintains that their exchange programs are not intended to serve a political purpose, however.

"China is committed to promoting mutual understanding and friendship between the Chinese and American peoples and advancing exchanges and cooperation between the two countries in areas including trade, education and culture," a spokesperson for the Chinese embassy in D.C. told Fox News Digital. "China opposes politicizing normal people-to-people, educational and economic exchanges. Such unfounded accusations serve no constructive purpose and do not contribute to the healthy development of China-U.S. relations."

"We hope the U.S. side will view China and bilateral relations in an objective and rational manner, provide an open, fair and non-discriminatory environment for exchanges and cooperation, and work together to promote the sound and stable development of China-U.S. relations," they added."

Fox News Digital reached out to the China Education Association for International Exchange for comment on the study, but did not receive a reply.

IF CHINA TARGETED OUR ELECTIONS, WHY REWARD IT WITH 600,000 STUDENT VISAS?

One 2025 newsletter published by the Chinese exchange program documents how 27 students from a high school in Chicago took a trip to the Chinese region of Xinjiang, where independent human rights organizations and the United States government say China is carrying out a genocide against Uyghur Muslims.

Despite the human rights abuses occurring in the province, visiting American students were provided with a rosy view of Xinjiang, taking dance classes, practicing calligraphy, doing Tai Chi and lounging at Heshuo Golden Beach.

FORMER CALIFORNIA MAYOR ADMITS TO SECRETLY WORKING FOR CHINA, SPREADING BEIJING PROPAGANDA IN US

If reactions from students and teachers who attend Young Envoys Scholarship trips are anything to go by, the Chinese government program has been successful in winning hearts and minds.

"I am a China fan," one high school student said after participating in a Young Envoys Scholarship program.

"President Xi Jinping’s message is very heartwarming," another student stated. A teacher said that she "strongly agreed with President Xi Jinping’s message that ‘the future is in the hands of the youth.'"

China makes use of these quotes, as well as others from similar trips, in articles produced by its state-run media organizations, which the United States government and some academics have described as "propaganda."

Chinese exchange programs are already on the radar of congressional China hawks.

"It is a tool used by the CCP to expand its influence over the American public," House Select Committee on the CCP Chairman John Moolenaar wrote in August 2025, addressing a school district in Maryland participating in an exchange program. "American youths should not be used as propaganda tools of the Chinese government to legitimize its authoritarian control or assert its undue influence on the American population."

item.title: Dem Senate nominee admits 'I take responsibility' after police report alleges he broke down door, punched man
item.description: Troy Jackson acknowledged a 1988 fight, and the NRSC called on Senate Democrats to condemn the Democrat nominee challenging Susan Collins in Maine.
item.content:encoded:
Maine Democratic Senate nominee Troy Jackson acknowledged to Fox News Digital that he got into a fight with another man nearly four decades ago, and Senate Republicans reacted to a newly surfaced police report detailing the violent confrontation.

"Nearly 40 years ago, when I was 19 years old, I got into a fight with another man. I took responsibility for it then, and I take responsibility for it now," Jackson told Fox News Digital.

"But let me be clear: I have never been violent with my partner Lana, or any other woman," Jackson added. "This happened nearly four decades ago, and I assure Mainers this incident in no way reflects the man I am today or the life I’ve led in the years since."

FORMER PLATNER ALLY TROY JACKSON LOCKS DOWN DELEGATES AS TOP RIVALS FOR DEMOCRATIC SENATE NOMINATION DROP OUT

The National Republican Senatorial Committee (NRSC) is calling on Democrats to condemn Jackson over the report as he campaigns to unseat Republican Sen. Susan Collins in a race that could help determine control of the Senate.

"Disgusting and inexcusable," the NRSC wrote in a post on X. "Troy Jackson is violent, unhinged, and has no place in the Senate."

The NRSC also tagged a handful of Senate Democrats in posts specifically mentioning the 1988 incident, including Sheldon Whitehouse, D-R.I.; Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y.; Kirsten Gillibrand, D-N.Y.; Chris Murphy, D-Conn.; Ruben Gallego, D-Ariz.; and Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass. 

The NRSC also tagged Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt.; former North Carolina Gov. Roy Cooper; and former Sen. Sherrod Brown, D-Ohio.

The Bangor Daily News first obtained and reported on the 1988 Fort Kent Police Department report, which the outlet said describes Jackson breaking down a door and punching a man at a Fort Kent home.

According to the newspaper's account of the police report and a handwritten witness statement, Jackson went to the home shortly before 2 a.m. March 12, 1988. After an occupant told him to leave, Jackson allegedly "kicked the door in."

INTERNET ERUPTS OVER REPORT THAT PLATNER'S REPLACEMENT IN KEY SENATE RACE FATHERED CHILDREN WITH SECOND COUSIN

Jackson then allegedly grabbed the man by the throat and swung at him, striking his glasses and cutting his face, according to the BDN's account of the records. The witness said Jackson warned the man to "stay away from Lana Pelletier or else."

The police report also notes Pelletier, Jackson's longtime partner, told an officer that Jackson had pushed her after the confrontation and that she planned to seek "cease harassment papers," according to the BDN.

Pelletier disputed that account in a statement to Fox News Digital.

"I do not remember making the statements attributed to me, and they are not accurate. This is the first time I have seen this report from 40 years ago," Pelletier said. "Troy and I have built a life and family together, and I know the person he has been through the decades since, both as a caring partner and father."

The BDN reported that it found no record Pelletier ever sought such an order.

A surviving court summary shows Jackson entered into an agreement to pay the man $50 to resolve the case, according to the BDN. The newspaper reported that the underlying court file has since been destroyed under the state's records-retention schedule.

The BDN also reported that its background check found Jackson does not have a criminal record and that the 1988 case was the only criminal case it located involving him.

Fox News Digital has made multiple attempts to independently obtain the underlying records and contacted the Fort Kent Police Department and District Court seeking the original police report. Fox News Digital additionally submitted a request through Maine's state criminal background check system, finding no viewable corresponding results.

The controversy comes shortly after Jackson secured the Democratic nomination to challenge Collins following the collapse of Graham Platner's ill-fated campaign.

Fox News Digital also reached out to Sen. Collins' office for comment.

item.title: Innocent wrestling with sister of wife's best friend reveals cheating with a twist, McDonald's wedding & signs
item.description: Nicole Kidman says she's embracing love after her divorce from Keith Urban, plus a wild slip 'n slide affair story and a McDonald's wedding in Ohio.
item.content:encoded:
We've survived another week, and we're here for another edition of True Romance. I was planning to kick things off by taking another look at the training camp lack of focus being displayed by quarterbacks around the league.

I get there's a love story there, but I'm not going to get into that again. A headline popped up and slapped me across the face this morning that I couldn’t ignore. It's about Nicole Kidman.

She's, believe it or not, embracing love after her divorce from Keith Urban. My first thought is what a hero. But there's more to it than just that.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Kidman could actually be a reader of True Romance with what she had to say about her breakup. She told British Vogue, reports Page Six, "I've always wanted to live a well-examined life."

Okay, well not that part. I would never say anything so insightful. But as she goes on, she does hit on what it is I pretend we're doing every week.

"So what does that entail?" she continued. "Trying things, making mistakes, failing, getting back up, moving on, embracing love, staying open, keeping the heart open and the possibilities."

We usually save the emotional moments for somewhere towards the end or stuff them down and bury them entirely. Not this week. And we have Nicole Kidman to thank for that.

Go follow True Romance on Twitter and Facebook. Send your emails here: sean.joseph@outkick.com (anonymously if you prefer).

This twisted tale of romance gone afoul is a first for the column. Not the twisted romance or the going afoul. We've had those before.

I've also had writers and editors send stories my way before. I've had emails and, more recently, song suggestions from readers, but this is the first story sent in by a reader.

OutKick reader Guy sent in the story of how a Kentucky woman came home early from work on the Fourth of July and learned of her husband's affair thanks to a Slip 'N Slide wrestling match.

The woman's husband and her best friend's sister were the two involved in the bizarre scene. Spoiler alert, the best friend's sister is not who the husband was cheating on his wife with.

Britney shared her story on social media, reports MSN. She was working overtime on the Fourth of July when one of her best friends' sisters called and told her to come home and celebrate the holiday.

She did and when she arrived home, the celebration was already underway and her husband was holding her best friend in the air by the legs. She didn’t think anything of it and had no idea that things were only going to get weirder.

Britney was approached by another one of her best friend's sisters. She wanted to know if she could tackle her husband. The sister was wearing a baggy shirt and biker shorts at the time, so she agreed.

The best friend's sister tackled Britney's husband, then changed into a thong bikini and started wrestling with him on a Slip 'N Slide that was set up.

"They proceed to wrestle on the Slip ‘N Slide for, like, a good 30 minutes. Like, they’re going at it," Britney claimed. They were all over each other and everyone was watching.

The sister's fiancé wasn't happy about what he was witnessing and neither was Britney's best friend, which Britney was touched by. She assumed her best friend was upset on her behalf, because of her husband's behavior.

Then a joke about it being slippery by the husband went too far. She had decided that the marriage, which was already in trouble at that point, was over.

Britney later learned about the affair her husband was having. It wasn't with her best friend's engaged sister who he was wrestling with at the party.

The affair was with her best friend. That's why she was upset by the Slip 'N Slide entertainment. She wasn’t taking up for Britney at all. She was watching her man wrestle with her sister and didn’t like it.

There's no need to worry about Britney. She didn’t just end her marriage, she ended her friendship as well and she's gone on to find love again.

Isn't that a wholesome story about loving, losing, and having it all turning out in your favor again. Your marriage may end on a Slip 'N slide, but there's still love out there if you know where to look.

Follow True Romance on Twitter and Facebook.

I don't want any of the overrated fries at McDonald's. I don’t want much from the fast food establishment at all. But I'll take romance and an ice cream machine that works.

They have at least one of those at a location in Ohio where two coworkers tied the knot over the weekend. George and Jamie Callicoat were married in the dining room area of a McDonald's in Akron.

The location didn't completely close during the ceremony; that would be insane. Cleveland.com reports the dining room was closed to the public for two hours, from 5 to 7 pm. The drive-thru was open for business.

"This is so much more than a wedding at a McDonald’s," Tammy Snider, the general manager of the McDonald’s, Tammy Snider, said.

"It's a story about two people in love and a restaurant team that wanted to make sure they felt celebrated."

Well said. What more do you need?

You can blow an insane amount of money on a wedding and have two people enter into a marriage with a fraction of the love that was packed into that McDonald's on Saturday.

I'll take a McDonald's dining room wedding over a spectacle at Madison Square Garden any day. I'm going out on a limb here, but I'm guessing this one didn't have a disgusting prenup attached to it.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK CULTURE COVERAGE

Not every marriage is going to make it. That's reality. Some of the ones that end before the "death do us part" have early signs that they aren’t going to make it, even at the wedding.

These are some that were noticed by the good people of Reddit at the wedding that they, in some cases, appear to have kept to themselves. I'm not judging, I would do the same thing.

Sit back and watch it unfold. That's how you feel alive.

-------------

STAY "FEARLESS" ON THE GO! TAKE TOMI LAHREN WITH YOU. DOWNLOAD THE TLIF PODCAST NOW!

That's all I have this week. I'm heading out for a week-long vacation after I punch the clock later this evening, but there will be another True Romance next Thursday afternoon.

In the meantime, keep the song of the week suggestions coming. You can reach me, anonymously if you prefer, at sean.joseph@outkick.com.

item.title: Hasan Piker is becoming the 'face of the progressive movement,' former Democratic operative warns
item.description: Hasan Piker is becoming the face of the progressive movement, says former Democratic operative Evan Barker, who warns candidates against working with him.
item.content:encoded:
Controversial Twitch streamer Hasan Piker has found himself at the center of a debate about the direction of the Democratic Party and generations of voters to come. However, recently on his stream, which he does for hours every day, the far-left commentator has claimed the media is making him out to have more influence than he actually does.

Evan Barker, author of "Nothing Left: Confessions Of A Democratic Operative," disagrees with Piker's analysis of his own popularity — he has more than 3 million followers on Twitch and millions more across other social media accounts — pointing to the increasing number of candidates who have invited him to campaign with them.

"Why would these candidates have this desire to bring him into their state, to campaign alongside him if he wasn't influential, to hold press junkets with him, to invite him to barbecues? Like, why would they be doing that if he didn't have influence? Like, clearly, he does," Barker told Fox News Digital.

Barker is no stranger to Democratic politics. She raised tens of millions of dollars for Democratic candidates, campaigned for Hillary Clinton and worked for candidates backed by Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y.

EX-DEM OPERATIVE DETAILS 'NEW DONOR ESTABLISHMENT' BEHIND MAMDANI-ERA PROGRESSIVES: 'NOT FROM THE GRASSROOTS'

Barker eventually broke with the party in 2024, a journey she details in her new book. She told Fox News Digital that Democrats are "testing their limits with the popularity" in areas of the country that aren't deep blue, especially when campaigning with Piker.

"It's one thing to appear on somebody's podcast, it's another to have them come campaign for you," she said.

Piker's hours-long stream primarily focuses on politics. He has backed several candidates in the 2026 cycle, including Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed and Wisconsin gubernatorial candidate Francesca Hong. 

While El-Sayed won his primary race, Hong lost to Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley, who has since said he was not planning on campaigning with Piker.

Piker's long history of incendiary and far-left rhetoric has made him an easy target for Republicans. From his retracted comments about saying the U.S. "deserved" 9/11, to his praise of Chinese dictator Mao Zedong, and the hours of talking he does every day, there's no shortage of comments for which Piker and his allies could be held to account.

When asked what she would tell candidates who are thinking about campaigning with the Twitch streamer, Barker told Fox News Digital that she would advise against it.

"I would say that the juice isn't worth the squeeze," she said. "Yeah, you're trying to appeal to younger voters, you're trying to drive out your base, but how do you win a general election aligning with him?"

DEMOCRAT ESTABLISHMENT STRIKES BACK AS SOCIALIST CANDIDATE DOWNED IN BATTLEGROUND PRIMARY

While Barker has expressed skepticism about Piker, she said she often hears those on the left defend their relationship with the streamer by comparing him to another media personality: Joe Rogan.

During the 2024 campaign cycle, then-Vice President Kamala Harris was criticized for not appearing on Rogan's widely followed podcast while running for president, particularly after both now-Vice President JD Vance and now-President Donald Trump sat for interviews with him. Some have made the case that Piker could serve as an alternative to Rogan, but Barker disagrees.

"Hasan Piker is not at all like Joe Rogan, actually. So, the charm of Joe Rogan, what makes his show so powerful, is that he talks about politics sometimes. Politics is sometimes peppered into his conversations, but by and large, the majority of the time, he's not talking about politics," she said. "Whereas Hasan Piker, that's pretty much all he talks about."

She also noted that some of Piker's rhetoric that appeals to younger voters might not resonate with larger populations in parts of the country that are not deep blue.

"At the end of the day, I would remind these progressive candidates, it's not just about pleasing your staff, it's not just about pleasing, you know, the young people that are in this movement. If you want to win places like Wisconsin, if you want to win places like Michigan, you have to be patriotic," she said. "The Rust Belt is filled with hardworking patriotic Americans who don't feel the way that Hasan Piker does."

WISCONSIN DEMOCRATIC VOTERS CHALK SOCIALIST FRANCESCA HONG'S STUNNING LOSS UP TO ELECTABILITY CONCERNS

As Democrats weigh the consequences of backlash for campaigning with Piker against the access to younger voters that he brings, Barker says the streamer is quickly becoming well known offline as well. She argued that Piker is "probably the biggest podcaster, live streamer" that the Democrats have at their disposal.

"He's quickly becoming a household name. He's quickly becoming the face of the progressive movement," she said.

Barker acknowledged that some progressives may not be "comfortable" with Piker as a de facto leader, calling his rise a "monster that they've created themselves." She also compared the current moment to previous shifts within the progressive movement, arguing that figures and ideas once embraced by the left are later dismissed as excesses of an earlier era.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Barker pointed specifically to recent discussions of "Woke 1" after Ocasio-Cortez's invocation of the term last week, arguing that Democrats have yet to reckon with the consequences of that period around 2020, which was marked by a surge in racial identity politics and progressive groupthink.

"People's lives were ruined because of 'woke 1.' It wasn't just some mass delusion or mass hysteria that we all went through... It pushed people away from Democratic politics," she said.

Barker argued that Democrats' continued willingness to align with figures like Piker shows the party has yet to move beyond that period.

"I think that there needs to be a true reckoning in the progressive movement and in the Democratic Party for people to really be able to heal and move on from this," she said.

Fox News Digital reached out to Piker for comment.

item.title: Surrogate gives birth in Texas to baby with heart defect after parents requested abortion
item.description: Baby Gabriel was born Wednesday after surrogate McKenna West fled to Texas, where Attorney General Ken Paxton secured legal victory for surgery.
item.content:encoded:
A surrogate mother gave birth to a baby against its biological parents' wishes after fleeing to Texas with help from state Attorney General Ken Paxton.

Surrogate mother McKenna West fled to Texas after her baby was diagnosed with hypoplastic left heart syndrome around the time West was 20 weeks pregnant. The diagnosis allegedly prompted the baby's birth parents to ask West to have an abortion, Paxton's office wrote in a news release Tuesday.

After West went to Texas, Paxton intervened, formally notifying UT Southwestern Medical Center and Children’s Medical Center of Dallas of their legal obligations to provide the baby with "medically necessary, life-saving care upon birth," his office wrote.

DEM GOV MAURA HEALEY SIGNS SWEEPING MASSACHUSETTS BILL ALLOWING ABORTIONS UP TO BIRTH

"The court has made the right decision in immediately acting to protect baby Gabriel’s life and ensure he receives the care he deserves," Paxton said in the statement. 

"My office utilized every tool at our disposal to protect life, and we will not back down in continuing to support baby Gabriel’s well-being. Every child in our state deserves to be cared for and protected, and that’s exactly what I’ll fight for."

"While the surrogate mother of baby Gabriel has traveled to Texas for protection and care for Gabriel, the intended parents have refused to agree that they will consent to the life-saving surgery for Gabriel after he is born. Attorney General Paxton has now secured a legal victory that will ensure baby Gabriel’s life is protected and that care is provided," Paxton's office added.

West's baby, named Gabriel, was born Wednesday, according to Fox News' Kerri Urbahn. Gabriel was brought to a neonatal intensive care unit, where doctors could soon perform lifesaving surgery.

SUPREME COURT UNANIMOUSLY SLAPS DOWN BLUE STATE TARGETING PRO-LIFE GROUP

The hospital where the surgery would likely be performed has a 100% success rate on the procedure, Urbahn reported.

"Baby Gabriel deserves a chance at life, and I will not allow anyone to unlawfully deny him medically necessary care," Paxton said. "My office will use every tool available to protect innocent lives and ensure that every child receives the care required under Texas law."

Fox News Digital contacted Paxton's office, UT Southwestern Medical Center and Children’s Medical Center of Dallas for additional comment.

item.title: Socialist insurgency heads to Trump’s backyard, targets pro-Israel Democrat
item.description: The Democratic Party's ideological civil war moves to Florida, where DSA-endorsed Oliver Larkin challenges AIPAC-backed Rep. Jared Moskowitz.
item.content:encoded:
The high-stakes battle for the ideological future of the Democratic Party moves to Florida next week, before heading to New England early next month, as the 2026 primary season wraps up.

After impactful left-wing victories this month by Michigan's Abdul El-Sayed and Minnesota Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan in crucial Democratic Senate primaries, and a searing setback for the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), with the downing of DSA member Francesca Hong in Wisconsin's Democratic gubernatorial primary, the next faceoff in the party's civil war comes Tuesday in Florida.

That's where DSA endorsed Oliver Larkin is challenging more moderate Democratic Rep. Jared Moskowitz in a key congressional swing district that's among roughly two dozen House seats that will determine if Republicans hold onto their razor-thin majority in the midterm elections.

DEMOCRATIC GROUP LAUNCHES $15 MILLION WAR ON DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS: 'MORTAL DANGER'

Two weeks later, the party's divisions return to a statewide stage, as longtime progressive leader Sen. Ed Markey of Massachusetts is facing a serious primary challenge from more moderate Democratic Rep. Seth Moulton.

A left-versus-center battle is brewing a week later in neighboring New Hampshire, in the party's Senate primary for a crucial battleground seat Democrats must hold in the midterm elections in order to win back the chamber's majority from the GOP.

Progressives scored their biggest victory to date a week ago, when El-Sayed narrowly edged moderate Rep. Haley Stevens to capture the party's Senate nomination in the Great Lakes battleground, in the race to succeed retiring Democratic Sen. Gary Peters.

DEMOCRATIC GROUP LAUNCHES $15 MILLION WAR ON DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS: 'MORTAL DANGER'

On Tuesday, Flanagan downed moderate Democratic Rep. Angie Craig by roughly 20 points, to grab the party's nomination in blue-leaning but competitive Minnesota, in the race to succeed another retiring Democrat, Sen. Tina Smith.

Both El-Sayed and Flanagan were backed by top far-left leaders, including progressive champion Sen. Bernie Sanders of Vermont.

But in Wisconsin's Democratic gubernatorial showdown, Hong was upset by a razor-thin margin by Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley, who was backed by retiring Democratic Gov. Tony Evers.

Evers and Crowley, pointing to Hong's past controversial comments on defunding the police and criticizing Thanksgiving, argued that a Hong primary victory would have boosted GOP nominee Rep. Tom Tiffany's chances of flipping the Wisconsin governor's mansion.

With the primary calendar winding down, here's a closer look at the final nomination faceoffs that are dividing Democrats and giving Republicans plenty of ammunition to use in the midterms.

Florida

The 33-year-old Larkin, a veteran of Sanders' 2016 Democratic presidential campaign, is also the only DSA-endorsed House candidate running in a crucial congressional swing district.

Larkin says he supports abolishing the U.S. Senate, arguing in a Fox News interview that it's an "undemocratic institution."

He agreed with socialist New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu should have been arrested during his recent trip to the U.S., and refers to Israel's ruling coalition as a "religious supremacist regime."

Moskowitz is a strong and vocal supporter of Israel, who has advocated for robust U.S. military and security assistance.

DEMOCRACY ’26: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB

The two-term federal lawmaker and former state representative and Florida FEMA director is running for re-election in the state's newly redrawn 25th Congressional District, a Broward County-anchored seat in the southeastern corner of the red-leaning state.

Moskowitz, who enjoys establishment backing from the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee, is also supported by AIPAC, a major-Israel aligned political group. Larkin enjoys plenty of support from top far-left leaders, including controversial political streamer Hasan Piker. Moskowitz is the polling and fundraising lead over Larkin heading into the primary.

Massachusetts

Markey is backed by a slew of progressive politicians and groups, including Sanders and Sen. Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts, as well as fellow Bay Stater Rep. Ayanna Pressley, a member of the far-left Squad.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Moulton is supported by a smaller group of more moderate Democratic lawmakers and groups.

item.title: Luxury $9 million yacht caught on camera sinking off coast, days after delivery to owner
item.description: Video footage shows the $9.1 million Angiola II tipping onto its side in the Mediterranean Sea after engine failure sparked a fire off Porto Cervo.
item.content:encoded:
A luxury $9.1 million yacht sank into the waters of the Mediterranean Sea Tuesday, just days after it had been delivered to its new owner.

The Angiola II was off the coast of Porto Cervo on the popular Italian island of Sardinia with 14 guests on board when it experienced engine failure that sparked a fire, the New York Post reported.

The blaze damaged seals on the vessel, which began to take on water, causing it to tip onto its side.

DRUNK REPEAT OFFENDER CALLED A 'TICKING TIME BOMB' BEFORE 80-MPH BOATING COLLISION KILLED WOMAN: PROSECUTORS

The guests managed to escape to safety and were rescued by nearby vessels, The Telegraph reported.

Video footage showed the boat on its side.

COAST GUARD OPENS FIRE ON BOAT SMUGGLING 25 CHINESE NATIONALS NEAR FLORIDA AFTER IT REFUSED TO STOP

The unidentified owner — an Italian businessman — was the last one off the ship, the newspaper reported.

The yacht reportedly sank at a depth of around 23 feet between an island called L’Isola dei Cappuccini and Capo Ferro on Sardinia’s exclusive Costa Smeralda, or Emerald Coast, the news report states.

The boat will be kept under surveillance until a recovery company recovers it from the sea floor.

The yacht can reportedly accommodate 10 guests and is fitted with five cabins and five crew members. 

It has four engines and can reach speeds of 28 knots.

The pitch clock was brilliant. I've come around on the ghost runner. ABS has very clearly worked. The Home Run Derby and the All-Star game are the two best exhibition events in sports (not a high bar, to be fair).

Does it seem a bit ironic that MLB’s Field of Dreams game — which harkens back to a simpler, more bucolic time — is being streamed on Netflix?

item.title: Hasan Piker event cancellation sparks intervention from top House progressive

item.content:encoded:
A top House Democrat is speaking out against a university's decision to cancel an appearance by controversial far-left activist Hasan Piker on its campus.

Rep. Pramila Jayapal, D-Wash., the former Congressional Progressive Caucus chair, publicly called on students at the University of Washington to "work with the university to ensure" that Piker was able to speak.

Jayapal also said in a statement posted to X on Thursday that she was personally working with the university on the issue.

DEMOCRATIC INFIGHTING GROWS AS CONGRESSWOMAN EXPOSES ‘DISRESPECTFUL’ WELCOME OF SOCIALISTS INTO ‘BIG TENT’

"As a Member of the Judiciary Committee, I have been absolutely clear that free speech is a constitutional right that we must all stand up and protect. I have been communicating my concerns about the cancellation of the Hasan Piker event directly to the University, and they have informed me that they are doing an internal review to ensure this never happens again," Jayapal wrote.

Piker posted on X earlier this week that the event was canceled due to his criticism of Israel.

"i wish the dems were smarter & didn’t let the [right-wing] groups be the only people who speak out against this clear violation of [the First Amendment] but unfortunately my position as a prominent critic of israel stops them from using this moment to show gop as arch cancel culture warriors," Piker wrote.

Piker, a streamer, has long made headlines for controversial and far-left statements.

In 2019, he said "America deserved 9/11" over its foreign policy decisions, though he later walked it back on "The Young Turks," stating, "Every part of what I advocate for is against violence" and insisting his statement was misconstrued.

HASAN PIKER'S DEFENSE OF HAMAS HAVING 'RIGHT TO RESIST MILITARILY' DRAWS CONDEMNATION FROM HUMAN RIGHTS GROUPS

Piker said at a Yale University event in April 2026 that "the fall of the USSR was one of the greatest catastrophes of the 20th century."

The far-left activist and his past statements have been back in the national conversation in recent weeks as he campaigns with socialist-aligned candidates across the country. That includes Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed and failed Wisconsin gubernatorial candidate Francesca Hong.

item.title: Chicago Bears say 'sole focus' is building new stadium in Indiana and reveal how that will affect their name

item.content:encoded:
The Chicago Bears on Thursday announced their new stadium planning and expectations after considering options in Arlington Heights, Illinois, and Hammond, Indiana will now have a "sole focus" on the site in the state next door.

The club is definitely leaving Chicago, which it has called home since 1921.

"Even though we've had occasional meetings with the state of Illinois, our sole focus at this point in time is working on a world-class stadium and mixed-use development in Hammond, Indiana," Bears CEO Kevin Warren told reporters Thursday.

So, the Indiana Bears?

The Hammond Bears?

Nope.

"We will be the Chicago Bears, whether we're in Arlington or whether we're in Hammond," Bears Chairman George McCaskey said. "And, as Kevin said, our focus on Hammond, that's where we're advancing our efforts, and that's where the bulk of our time, attention and resources are being devoted."

McCaskey said he understands there is anxiety from Bears fans that the club is likely leaving the state.

"We understand that that's out there," he said. "And it needs to be dealt with. We are doing surveying, research, data collection to address those issues. And as I said months ago, this is going to require an adjustment.

"Minimal," McCaskey said, describing the communication. "We were waiting to see whether there would be some substantive action taken. We thought we had presented a pretty compelling case that a stadium in Arlington would be beneficial not only for the village of Arlington Heights, but for the community and for the entire state.

item.title: Resurfaced WNBA post shows league celebrating males who stole wins from female athletes
item.description: A resurfaced 2021 WNBA post celebrated trans athletes Andraya Yearwood and Terry Miller while the league now says it needs months to define eligibility.
item.content:encoded:
The WNBA apparently needs "weeks and months" to figure out whether biological males should be eligible to play in a professional basketball league for women.

Five years ago, the league didn't seem nearly as confused.

CLUELESS WNBA ATTACKS 'BAD-FAITH' FANS WHO DON'T WANT BIOLOGICAL MEN RUINING WOMEN'S SPORTS

A resurfaced June 2021 post from the WNBA’s official X (formerly Twitter) account, which was also shared on Facebook, celebrated Andraya Yearwood and Terry Miller, two males who competed in girls' high school track in Connecticut and were at the center of a major legal fight after beating female athletes in championship events.

"Our first #WCW of #WNBAPride goes out to Andraya Yearwood and Terry Miller," the WNBA wrote.

Yes, the Women's National Basketball Association used its first "Woman Crush Wednesday" of Pride Month to celebrate two males.

"We see you. We support you and all of the other trans athletes just trying to compete in the sports they love," the league added.

The post remains live on X and the same message is still posted on the WNBA's official Facebook account.

The WNBA knew who it was celebrating. Yearwood and Miller had already become nationally known for winning girls’ track titles and finishing ahead of female athletes in Connecticut.

Those girls had names, too.

Selina Soule. Chelsea Mitchell. Alanna Smith. Ashley Nicoletti.

Funny, the WNBA's post didn't mention them.

Yearwood began competing in girls' track in 2017 under Connecticut Interscholastic Athletic Conference rules and won the Class M state championship in both the 100- and 200-meter events that year. A federal district court ruling recounting the plaintiffs' allegations says Yearwood's advancement to the State Open displaced Chelsea Mitchell, a female, from qualifying.

Miller began competing in girls' track the following year. At the 2018 Outdoor State Open, Miller and Yearwood finished first and second in the girls' 100 meters. The court noted that Mitchell would have finished second statewide without their participation. Miller also won the 200 meters.

Then came 2019.

At the State Indoor Open, Miller and Yearwood finished first and second in both the preliminary and final 55-meter races. According to the court record, Mitchell would have won the final without them and Soule would have advanced to the next stage of competition. Later that spring, Miller won another state championship over Mitchell, while Miller also won the State Open 200-meter final ahead of Smith.

Nicoletti was affected, too. The plaintiffs sought revisions to 2019 race results that included events where Miller and Yearwood finished ahead of Nicoletti, along with numerous races where one or both finished ahead of Soule, Mitchell and Smith.

By the time the WNBA posted its support in 2021, there was no mystery about the controversy surrounding Yearwood and Miller. The post itself points to one reason why: the league credited Athlete Ally, an organization that had already honored both athletes at its 2019 Action Awards.

Athlete Ally’s announcement specifically noted that Yearwood had won the 100- and 200-meter dashes and that Miller had won the State Open 200-meter title for the second consecutive year. It also referenced the legal effort challenging their participation in girls’ track.

And guess who Athlete Ally listed among the supporters of those 2019 awards?

The NBA and WNBA.

WNBPA ISSUES STATEMENT EMBRACING DIVERSITY AND INCLUSION AMID TRANS ATHLETE DEBATE IN WOMEN'S SPORTS

Two years later, the WNBA officially partnered with Athlete Ally for Pride Month. A league press release said one of the WNBA/WNBPA Social Justice Council's priorities was LGBTQ advocacy "with a focus on trans rights," and the league announced that Athlete Ally would conduct educational sessions for WNBA teams on "trans inclusivity."

The WNBA was clearly on board with male participation in girls' and women’s sports.

Meanwhile, the girls who actually raced Yearwood and Miller were the ones dealing with the consequences.

Alliance Defending Freedom, which represents Soule, Mitchell, Smith and Nicoletti in their lawsuit against Connecticut officials, has published extensive accounts of what those girls say they lost while competing against males.

Mitchell was one of the best female sprinters in Connecticut. In 2019, she said she was "ranked the fastest biological female in the state of Connecticut," yet she had to repeatedly watch championship honors go to male competitors.

"When I have to compete against a transgender athlete, I just feel completely defeated before I even run the race," Mitchell said.

Think about that for a second.

Mitchell was fast enough to win state championships. In several championship races, she was the fastest female on the track, yet the title still went to a male competitor.

Soule described realizing the problem almost immediately when she first raced against a male athlete as a freshman.

"I knew right then and there that some girls will be missing out on great opportunities to succeed, and that women could be completely eradicated from their own sports," she said.

In the 2019 indoor State Open, Miller and Yearwood took the top two spots while Soule missed advancing.

The consequences went beyond titles and qualifying spots. For Ashley Nicoletti, simply lining up against a male competitor changed how she viewed the race before it even started.

"I felt nervous even at the thought of such an unfair race," Nicoletti told ADF. "I knew I had a chance against other girls, but not against a male athlete."

Those were the girls losing titles and opportunities while the WNBA was backing athletes like Yearwood and Miller.

Mitchell lost championship recognition; Soule lost an opportunity to advance; and, Nicoletti described knowing before the race even started that she couldn't fairly compete.

Yet the WNBA's message to Yearwood and Miller was: "We see you. We support you."

Where was that support for the girls who actually lost to them?

And then there's Alanna Smith.

Miller finished ahead of Smith in championship competition, including winning the 200-meter final at the 2019 State Open. ADF recounts a conversation between Smith and her mother on the way to a meet in New York City. Her mother asked what her strategy was going to be that day.

Smith's response?

"Mom, it really doesn't matter, because I'm running against the boys today."

Fast-forward five years, and that certainty is gone. Male participation in women’s sports is now apparently a question requiring extended consultation.

On paper, the new collective bargaining agreement appears to provide a clear answer: "Only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA."

Except the 409-page agreement doesn’t define "woman," and the league has repeatedly declined to tell OutKick/Fox News Digital whether a biological male who identifies as a woman would satisfy that requirement.

The issue escalated after former NBA players Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White announced that they planned to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft, directly challenging the league's undefined eligibility language.

The WNBA convened a task force this week amid pressure to answer the question. It emerged without a definition and said it would spend the coming "weeks and months" continuing discussions with league stakeholders.

But here's the part that really tells the story.

A source familiar with the league and with Wednesday's meeting told Fox News that the meeting "focused significantly on the hate and vitriol being directed at WNBA players online."

So, amid mounting questions about who is eligible to compete in a women’s league, the WNBA spent a significant portion of its meeting discussing "hate and vitriol" directed at players online.

That’s the priority?

RILEY GAINES SAYS WNBA IS 'HELLBENT' ON BEING AN ACTIVIST ORGANIZATION OVER A BASKETBALL LEAGUE

The WNBA’s sudden concern about the tone of the conversation is pretty rich. Criticism of the league’s eligibility policy isn’t the same thing as hatred, and asking whether males should be eligible to compete against women isn’t "demeaning" anyone.

Four female athletes told the world that they were losing championships, advancement opportunities and recognition because they were being forced to compete against males. The WNBA didn't issue a statement expressing concern for their well-being. It didn't announce that it needed to engage stakeholders to make sure female athletes were being treated fairly.

It celebrated the males who beat them.

WNBA star Sophie Cunningham put the issue in plain terms, saying girls shouldn’t have to "go against biological men."

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS

But the league still hasn’t said whether a biological male could be eligible to play in the WNBA.

STAY "FEARLESS" ON THE GO! TAKE TOMI LAHREN WITH YOU. DOWNLOAD THE TLIF PODCAST NOW!

In 2021, while males Andraya Yearwood and Terry Miller were taking titles and opportunities from girls, the WNBA publicly backed them.

"We see you. We support you."

The girls they beat got a very different message.

item.title: Social media has a field day with Texas A&M player for looking like a 36-year-old construction worker
item.description: Texas A&M defensive end Anto Saka thanked strength coach Tommy Moffitt for his offseason gains, but his mature looks had social media in disbelief.
item.content:encoded:
Offseason transformations are one of the coolest parts about college football.

It's simply amazing to see what six to eight months in a Division I strength and conditioning program can do for a group of young men, especially considering that, for the majority of them, this is the first time they've seriously thrown some weight around in their lives.

OKLAHOMA SOONERS QUARTERBACK JOHN MATEER LOOKS ABSOLUTELY JACKED JUST IN TIME FOR FALL CAMP

I'm not sure what Moffitt and the Aggies are putting in their post-workout protein shakes, though, because Saka's mature looks caught the eye of the entire internet earlier this week.

You're trying to tell me that's a college kid? Because he looks like a 36-year-old construction worker with two kids and a mortgage.

I know redshirt rules have gotten a little out of hand in college sports recently, but there's no way this 30-something union worker has any eligibility left to play football.

Sure, Jan.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL COACHES ON HOT SEAT: BILL BELICHICK, MIKE NORVELL AND OTHERS FACING MAKE-OR-BREAK 2026

Social media had an absolute field day with Saka, dropping memes left and right poking fun at the world's oldest looking guy who can't legally rent a car yet.

If Hollywood were to cast this young man to portray a college student in a movie, we would all collectively complain about how they never get actors to play characters their age.

He's like a real-life Luke Perry in "90210."

Anyway, congrats on the big gains in the weight room, Anto!

item.title: Pro wrestling icon Matt Hardy puts first tag team ladder match in historical perspective
item.description: Matt Hardy reveals the 1999 tag team ladder match with Edge and Christian that he says launched the TLC concept and changed pro wrestling forever.
item.content:encoded:
Whichever version of Matt Hardy a pro wrestling fan may have enjoyed over the course of his more than 35 years in the sport, his innovative mind and versatile in-ring abilities may be what he will be remembered for most when he finally decides to hang up his boots.

Hardy has been a scene stealer in almost every company he’s worked for, whether it was WWE, All Elite Wrestling (AEW), Total Nonstop Action Wrestling (TNA), Ring of Honor or elsewhere.

The 51-year-old multi-time champion has done nearly everything in the business. 

COMPLETE PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE ON FOX NEWS DIGITAL

Fox News Digital asked Hardy in a recent interview which moment of his career he thought isn't talked about enough. Hardy pointed to the first-ever tag team ladder match he and his brother, Jeff, had with Edge and Christian at No Mercy 1999.

He said the match helped pave the way for the historic tables, ladders and chairs match that took place at SummerSlam 2000 and innovated the way inanimate objects are used in the wrestling ring.

"It’s crazy because my brother and I, we've been blessed to have so many great moments over our — Oct. 15 we'll be going into our 35th year of doing this as pro wrestlers, which is crazy," Hardy said. 

"A moment still that I don't think gets talked about quite enough — it got praised, especially when it happened — but just looking back at how monumental it was in changing the game was the first-ever tag team ladder match, I think.

BZZR 'CUTTING OUT THE NOISE' FROM SPORTS SOCIAL MEDIA SPACE GREAT FOR CREATORS, SPORTSCASTER JON ALBA SAYS

"I still think it was so instrumental in leading the way for change in the way of telling stories with inanimate objects in WWE because that ultimately led to us doing the first-ever tag team tables match with the Dudleys, which is an idea I presented to Vince (McMahon). He wanted to do something with the Dudleys that paralleled what we did with Edge and Christian. 

"And then that led to us using all of these items in WrestleMania 2000 and then, ultimately, at SummerSlam 2000, we did the first ever TLC, tables, ladders and chairs match and that has become a staple in pro wrestling and even in other companies."

Hardy pointed to other companies using similar matches, including AEW, TNA’s Full Metal Mayhem and Ring of Honor’s Ladder Wars.

"But that tag team ladder match that we did with Edge and Christian is something that was, like, absolutely the beginning and origin point of the TLC concept. And that became a staple in pro wrestling. And, myself and Jeff and Edge and Christian, without us having that match, that doesn't become a thing.

"So, that is a moment, I think, historically, years down the road, decades down the road, people will look back at that, and they go, ‘Wow, that was the moment where all of this insanity started.’ And there was a different way of telling stories with these inanimate objects doing a different version of storytelling, doing a different version of match that can be exciting and athletic guys can really benefit from it."

Now, as his career reaches 35 years, Hardy and his brother are the TNA world tag team champions. He also hosts a podcast with Jon Alba, sharing stories and memories from his career.

"The Extreme Life of Matt Hardy" drops a new episode each Friday on his YouTube page.

item.title: The scammer at your doctor's office may already know who you are
item.description: QR code scams at doctor's offices use data brokers and people search websites to craft personalized phishing attacks targeting your Medicare number.

You arrive at your doctor’s office and see a sign asking you to scan a QR code to check in. Later, you receive a text about a prescription. A Medicare notice with your name and address arrives in the mail. Before you leave, another QR code asks you to pay for parking. 

All of it looks routine. That’s exactly what can make these scams so dangerous. Criminals aren’t limited to sending obvious phishing messages to random people. Personal information available through data brokers and people search websites can help scammers create medical, Medicare and payment scams that look like they were meant specifically for you.

Then a QR code gives them an easy way to send you to a convincing fake website asking for your Medicare number, patient portal login, credit card information or other sensitive data. Here’s what to watch for during your next trip to the doctor’s office and one important step that can make you harder for scammers to target in the first place.

QR codes have become a normal part of healthcare. Doctors’ offices use them for check-in forms. Pharmacies use them for pickup information. Medicare Advantage and Part D plans may include them in enrollment materials and other communications. Hospitals and medical buildings increasingly use QR codes for parking payments. That familiarity works in a scammer’s favor. When you’re standing inside your doctor’s office holding paperwork that looks official or looking at a sign next to a parking machine, you naturally expect the information to be legitimate. Scammers know that.

A QR code also hides something that a normal web link does not: where it is actually taking you. You can usually glance at a link in an email before clicking it. With a QR code, you see a square filled with black and white patterns. You don’t know where it leads until your phone reads it. That makes the location of the QR code itself part of the deception.

The mechanics of the scam are surprisingly simple.

A criminal can:

Scan the code, and you may land on a website designed to resemble your insurer, pharmacy, doctor’s portal or payment processor.

The site may ask for your:

QR code phishing is sometimes called "quishing." The challenge is that many people have become so accustomed to QR codes that scanning one no longer feels like clicking a link.

This is where these scams can become much more convincing. A criminal contacting you may already have access to details such as your:

Some of that information can appear on data broker and people search websites. Think about the difference between receiving a generic message that says: "Your health coverage has changed" and receiving a notice addressed to you by name, sent to your correct home address and written to resemble something connected to Medicare or your health coverage. The second message feels far more believable. That’s why protecting yourself isn’t only about spotting a fake QR code. It's also about reducing the amount of personal information strangers can easily find about you online.

FAKE VA SHOE OFFER TARGETS VETERANS

These examples show how fraudulent QR codes can blend into places where people already expect to see them.

One Medicare beneficiary described receiving a letter that appeared to come from a major insurer and directed the recipient to scan a QR code to read an Annual Notice of Change. The letter reportedly closely resembled legitimate plan correspondence, but the QR code pointed to a shortened, lookalike web address instead of the insurer’s actual domain. This particular example is a reported account rather than a confirmed investigated incident, but it follows a familiar scam pattern: make an official-looking Medicare communication feel urgent and legitimate, then direct the victim somewhere controlled by the scammer.

At Totnes Community Hospital in the U.K., a fraudulent QR code sticker was discovered on a parking payment machine. One visitor who scanned the code to pay reportedly had £146.79 taken from her account. The scammers then attempted to take another £849 before her bank’s fraud team intervened. The hospital trust confirmed the fraudulent code and began monitoring payment machines at other locations.

Law enforcement in Redondo Beach and San Clemente, California, has documented scammers placing counterfeit QR code stickers next to legitimate parking payment instructions. A medical office or hospital parking structure can be an especially convincing place for this trick because people already expect to scan something to pay.

Older Americans frequently interact with healthcare systems, pharmacies, insurance providers and Medicare.

That means a message about a doctor's appointment, prescription pickup, Medicare coverage, insurance changes, medical paperwork or hospital parking may not seem unusual. Add accurate personal information to the message, and the scam can become even harder to recognize. That’s the real danger. The QR code might be the thing you scan, but the personal details surrounding it are what can make you trust it.

A few quick checks can help you determine whether a QR code deserves your trust.

Most modern phones display the destination before opening a QR code link. Look carefully at the web address. If the domain is unfamiliar, shortened, misspelled or slightly different from the organization’s normal website, don't continue.

If a receptionist, sign or piece of paperwork tells you to scan a QR code, there's nothing wrong with asking, "Is this your official QR code?" That simple question can protect you if someone has placed a fraudulent sticker over a legitimate code.

Before scanning a QR code on a sign, parking meter or payment machine, look closely. Be suspicious if the code:

An official-looking envelope does not guarantee that what’s inside is legitimate. If a Medicare or insurance notice tells you to scan a QR code, consider going directly to the organization’s known website instead. You can also call the phone number printed on your insurance card rather than relying on contact information supplied in an unexpected mailing.

FCC ROBOCALL CRACKDOWN COULD CHANGE PHONE PRIVACY

Whenever possible, use your healthcare provider’s official app or type its known website address directly into your browser. The same rule applies to Medicare, pharmacies and insurers. Don’t trust a QR code simply because it appears in a place you trust.

Enable two-factor authentication (2FA) for accounts that support it, especially:

Two-factor authentication adds another barrier even if a scammer manages to obtain your password.

Install operating system, browser and security updates when they become available. Updates can help protect against dangerous websites, malicious downloads and other threats you might encounter after scanning a fraudulent code.

If you see a QR code at a doctor’s office, hospital, pharmacy or parking facility that appears suspicious, tell an employee. Removing one fraudulent sticker could prevent many other people from scanning it. You can also report suspected fraud to the Federal Trade Commission at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.

Spotting a fraudulent QR code can protect you from one scam. Reducing the personal information available about you can make it harder for scammers to build convincing attacks in the first place. Data brokers and people search websites can expose information such as your name, address, phone number, age range and household details. Those pieces of information may seem harmless on their own. Put together, they can give a criminal enough background information to make a Medicare notice, medical message or other scam feel surprisingly personal.

You can contact data brokers and people search sites yourself and request that your information be removed. The challenge is that your information may appear across many different sites and can sometimes return after it has been removed.

A personal data removal service can help automate that process by sending removal requests to data brokers on your behalf and continuing to check whether your information reappears. No service can guarantee that every piece of personal information will disappear from the internet, but reducing what is easily available can give scammers fewer details to work with when trying to create a convincing, personalized attack.

Whether you handle removals yourself or use a service, periodically search for your name, phone number and address online to see what strangers can find. The less information that is readily available about you, the harder it can be for a scammer to make a fake medical message, Medicare notice or payment request look legitimate.

They may include your name, address or other accurate personal details that make a fake medical notice, Medicare communication or payment request feel legitimate. A QR code at your doctor’s office, in a healthcare mailing or on a hospital parking machine can simply be the final step that sends you to a fraudulent website. 

Before scanning, check the destination, look for signs of tampering and confirm unfamiliar codes with staff. Whenever possible, go directly to the organization’s official website or app. Just as importantly, find out how much personal information about you is publicly available online. The less information scammers can easily find about you, the harder it becomes for them to create a scam that feels like it was made specifically for you.

item.title: Beer, wine or liquor? Massive study reveals which was linked to lower death risk
item.description: Heavy alcohol use raised death risk by 24%, but wine at low levels was linked to lower mortality than beer or spirits in a UK Biobank study.
item.content:encoded:
Heavy drinking has been shown to raise mortality risk, but, at lower levels, what’s in your glass may also matter, a new study suggests.

In recent research of data from 340,924 participants in the UK Biobank, wine was linked to lower mortality, while beer and spirits were tied to higher death risk.

Data were collected between 2006 and 2022, with more than 13 years of average follow-up. The findings were presented at the American College of Cardiology’s Annual Scientific Session in New Orleans.

WINE EXPERT SAYS ONE COMMON HABIT COULD BE SABOTAGING EVERY SIP

In the study, participants reported their alcohol intake as never/occasional, low, moderate or high.

High consumption was defined as more than 40 grams per day for men (about three standard drinks) and more than 20 grams per day for women (about 1.4 standard drinks).

Participants with high alcohol consumption had a 24% higher risk of all-cause death, 36% higher risk of cancer death and 14% higher risk of cardiovascular death when compared to people who never or occasionally drank, according to the study findings.

With low or moderate alcohol consumption, however, the mortality risk appeared to differ according to the type of beverage.

AMERICA HITS MAJOR MARIJUANA MILESTONE AS DAILY WEED USE SURPASSES DAILY DRINKING

Spirits, beer and cider were associated with significantly higher mortality, the researchers found, while the same amount of wine intake was linked to significantly lower mortality. Moderate wine drinkers had a 21% lower risk of cardiovascular death than those who never or occasionally drank.

Conversely, those who drank low amounts of spirits, beer or cider were found to have a 9% higher risk of cardiovascular death.

"These results come from the general population, and in certain high-risk groups, such as people with chronic diseases or cardiovascular conditions, the risks could be even higher," Dr. Zhangling Chen, a professor at the Second Xiangya Hospital, Central South University in China and the study's senior author, said in a press release.

"These findings can help refine guidance, emphasizing that the health risks of alcohol depend not only on the amount of alcohol consumed but also on the type of beverage."

One potential reason for wine’s lower mortality association could be that it contains compounds such as polyphenols and antioxidants, which could have beneficial effects on blood vessels, inflammation and cardiovascular health, the researchers noted.

Jessica Steinman, a Los Angeles addiction specialist and chief clinical officer for No Matter What Recovery, said the study’s information is "helpful" but cautioned against broadly applying the findings to individuals, particularly those with a history of substance misuse.

HOME COCKTAIL MAKER SAYS GEN Z ISN'T GIVING UP ALCOHOL — THEY'RE CHANGING HOW THEY DRINK

While certain ingredients or substances might help someone with a specific issue, she expressed her concern when it comes to mental health issues and addiction.

"When we hear these stories or get this research, it becomes a ‘black and white’ larger generalization for the population, and we want to be careful with that," Steinman, who was not involved in the research, told Fox News Digital.

"Not everybody should have daily consumption of an alcoholic substance, whether it's wine, beer or certain liquors. … If there's someone who’s struggling with substances, then they really shouldn't be having it at all."

Different substances have different levels of alcohol in them, and each person metabolizes alcohol uniquely, the expert noted.

"All those kinds of things are so specific to one person or a small sect of people," she said. "So, we want to make sure anytime there's research given about something, that we're not taking it as a society and saying, ‘Let's do this,’ and not keeping it as black and white.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

"Overall, more is not better, but also the higher potency of alcohol and higher percentages of alcohol is going to affect people negatively as well."

Steinman recommended consulting with a medical professional for individual guidance.

The researchers acknowledged some limitations of the study. Because it was observational in design, the study could not prove that drinking wine led to lower mortality or that other alcoholic beverages directly caused higher mortality.

Also, the participants reported their baseline alcohol intake at the start of the study, which means any changes in drinking patterns during the follow-up period were not recorded.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

There was also the chance that wine drinkers may have different dietary or other lifestyle habits that could affect their health outcomes, the researchers noted.

The UK Biobank participants also tend to be healthier than the overall population, which could limit the ability for the finding to be generalized to wider populations.

The authors called for high-quality randomized studies to confirm the differences in how drinking habits reflect mortality risk.

item.title: 'Look at me!' Justice fires back at critics who dare question his Blackness
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Clarence Thomas reveals how Thomas Sowell's work freed him from isolation and gave him confidence to challenge Black political norms.
item.content:encoded:
Supreme Court Justice Clarence Thomas said his views on race and politics have led critics to question his Blackness.

"I mean, how stupid is that? Look at me," Thomas said, grabbing his arm. "You know, then they say things like, ‘Oh, black is a state of mind.’"

Thomas made the remarks during a Hoover Institution conversation with Peter Robinson that included a discussion about the role of Black Americans in politics. The conservative justice reflected on how economist Thomas Sowell, a Black conservative, helped transform his thinking on race and politics and gave him the confidence to challenge prevailing expectations about Black Americans' political views.

CLARENCE THOMAS WARNS AMERICA: LIBERTY DIES WHEN WE CHOOSE COMFORT OVER COURAGE

Thomas said that as a young man, he felt pressure to embrace certain political beliefs because he was Black and faced resistance when he began questioning them.

"You have these views, you have these instincts, but you are getting inputs from the media, from the politicians, the people who have the megaphone, the people who have the loudest voices, that tells you you’re wrong, that tells you you’re bad, that there’s something awful about you," Thomas said.

While at Yale Law School, Thomas said he bucked the push for school busing, questioning why Black families would want their children sent across town to unfamiliar schools and neighborhoods.

"I remember saying those things at Yale and people — the bottom line was, well, you shouldn’t believe that because you’re black," Thomas said.

KEY TRUMP AGENCY PUTS TOP UNIVERSITIES IN CROSSHAIRS OVER ALLEGED RACE-BASED DORM PROGRAMS

Thomas argued there was often a disconnect between positions championed by Black political leaders and the views of ordinary Black Americans, pointing to debates over school busing and racial preferences.

"If you ask the leaders, they thought one thing. If you ask the people, they thought another," Thomas said.

It was Sowell’s work, Thomas said, that helped him make sense of views he had already begun developing on his own.

A friend introduced Thomas to Sowell’s Race and Economics, which Thomas said helped free him from the isolation he had felt over his own views.

THE WELFARE STATE BROKE BLACK FAMILIES. WORK CAN HELP RESTORE THE DREAM

"It was literally like a drink of water," Thomas said. "Here’s someone who’s thought it through and it makes sense. What your instincts were have been now demonstrated in a logical, analytical way. You’re not alone." He later sought out a friendship with Sowell.

But Thomas had not always embraced Sowell’s ideas.

As a Yale student in 1972, Thomas said he "reflexively" rejected Sowell’s Black Education: Myths and Tragedies, believing that "no black man" should think that way.

Thomas said Sowell’s example helped give him the confidence to voice his own beliefs even when doing so brought criticism.

THOMAS LEAVES NOTHING LEFT UNSAID ON RACIAL GERRYMANDERING DECISION: ‘GO FURTHER’

"If they can prove you wrong, fine," Thomas said. "But if they call you names or say you’re not black, I mean, how stupid is that? Look at me."

He tied those attacks to what he described as a broader pressure on Black Americans to conform to certain views.

"There’s this overriding public view that you’re not supposed to think this way, therefore you’re not black, therefore you’re discredited," Thomas said. "Nothing you say matters."

But for Thomas, the biggest lesson he took from Sowell was to think for himself.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

"He always says what he thinks, but he never tells you to say what he wants you to think," Thomas said of Sowell. "That is yours."

"There seems to be this overwhelming pressure for us to agree with the prevailing notions which I consider almost illusory in a sense," Thomas said.

item.title: Scramble for Karoline Leavitt's replacement ensues with just weeks until Trump's spokesperson exits
item.description: Alina Habba, Stephen Miller and Scott Jennings are among the names floated to replace Karoline Leavitt as Trump's White House press secretary.
item.content:encoded:
The impending departure of President Donald Trump's top spokeswoman has speculation swirling in Washington, D.C., on who will be selected to replace Karoline Leavitt behind the press briefing room podium.

The 28-year-old White House press secretary, fresh off maternity leave, dropped a bombshell announcement on Wednesday that she will end her tenure at the end of August to spend more time with her two young children.

Now, with just two weeks left in the month, the race is on to find the next press secretary — and some predict the briefing room will see a rotating line of Trump administration officials briefing the White House press corps rather than a permanent replacement, like what happened during Leavitt's maternity leave earlier this summer.

WHITE HOUSE PLANS GUEST HOSTS FOR PRESS BRIEFINGS WHILE KAROLINE LEAVITT TAKES MATERNITY LEAVE

Secretary of State Marco Rubio held the first news conference while Leavitt was on leave, followed by Vice President JD Vance, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz.

"The next press secretary will undoubtedly be someone who has a strong existing relationship with President Trump," former Trump press secretary Sean Spicer told Fox News Digital.

"He values and understands the importance of this role in communicating his positions on policy, personnel and key issues, so I can’t imagine it not being someone currently in his orbit," Spicer added.

Spicer, known for his short tenure as White House press secretary, withdrew his name for consideration a second time around.

Alina Habba, who serves as senior advisor to the attorney general for U.S. Attorneys, was viewed as a frontrunner after Trump won re-election and is once again being floated for the role.

TRUMP SAYS KAROLINE LEAVITT WILL LEAVE WHITE HOUSE PRESS SECRETARY ROLE, BECOME OUTSIDE ADVISOR

At the time, Habba said she was "flattered" by the consideration but believed she would "be better served in other capacities."

She then served three months as counselor to the president before leaving Washington, D.C., for a controversial and turbulent position as interim attorney for the District of New Jersey. After her appointment was deemed unconstitutional, she resigned and was made senior advisor to the attorney general for United States Attorneys.

Habba, who was Trump's personal attorney and a high-profile surrogate on the 2024 campaign trail, was the early favorite on Kalshi to replace the press secretary but now ranks third behind conservative political commentator Scott Jennings and Leavitt's deputy, Anna Kelly.

Trump's principal deputy press secretary has been seen in an outward facing role. Kelly filled in for Leavitt in media hits while Leavitt was on maternity leave but has yet to take the podium for a briefing.

Jennings, a CNN contributor and former aide to President George W. Bush, was also reportedly considered for the press secretary role when Trump retook office in 2024 before he selected Leavitt. Trump has touted Jennings’ recent book and has referred to him as a "patriot" who "gets it."

TRUMP’S DC LAW-AND-ORDER BLITZ MARKS ONE YEAR WITH EYE-POPPING HAUL OF SUSPECTS

Trump's senior advisor, Stephen Miller, and his wife, Katie Miller, have been floated on social media as potential replacements.

Stephen was asked Wednesday for his thoughts on his wife, former Vice President Mike Pence's press secretary and communications director, filling Leavitt’s role. In lieu of commenting, he shot a smile in the direction of the questioner.

White House communication director Stephen Cheung is one of Trump’s most forceful defenders, wielding significant influence but largely operating behind the scenes.

Other names floated as potential contenders include Breitbart's Washington Bureau Chief Matthew Boyle and former White House deputy chief of staff Taylor Budowich.

Leavitt is Trump’s second-longest-serving press secretary with 19 months in the role. She comes in second to first-term press secretary and now Arkansas Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders’ 23-month tenure.

After Huckabee's departure, Stephanie Grisham stepped into the role for nine months but was famous for not holding a single press briefing during that time. She was eventually replaced with Kayleigh McEnany, who served through the end of Trump's first term.
